analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר, and יְהִי אוֹר (“Let there be light”) gives the words God spoke.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים, the third-person masculine singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר agrees with אֱלֹהִים as a single speaker. God gives the command יְהִי אוֹר, “Let there be light.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In God’s command יְהִי אוֹר, אוֹר (“light”) is the subject. The following וַיְהִי אוֹר (“and there was light”) reports the fulfillment of the command.
analysis.morphology: Qal jussive, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אוֹר.

analysis.evidence: In יְהִי אוֹר, “let there be light,” אוֹר is the subject of the masculine singular jussive יְהִי. The following וַיְהִי אוֹר, “and there was light,” confirms what came into being.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, used here with masculine singular agreement. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The command יְהִי אוֹר, “let there be light,” is followed by וַיְהִי אוֹר, “and there was light.” The marked verb narrates the fulfillment of the command, with אוֹר as its subject.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי אוֹר (“and there was light”), אוֹר is the subject of וַיְהִי. It names the light called for in יְהִי אוֹר (“let there be light”).
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
